claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
The Artemis II crew was recovered by a joint team aboard the USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10, 2026.
The spacecraft was the Orion spacecraft ("Integrity").
The recovery team consisted of NASA and U.S. Navy personnel aboard the USS John P. Murtha.
Artemis II was the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew returned safely after a 10-day trip
